name: Parikia
tagline: The port town, the island's practical centre year-round
description: Where the ferries dock and where the island actually functions: banks, the health centre, supermarkets, the old market lanes behind the waterfront and the Ekatontapyliani church. It stays open through the winter, which most of the island does not, and it has the best transport links to everywhere else.
bestFor: Anyone staying past the season who needs a town that keeps working
pros: Everything open year-round, including services and supermarkets
All bus routes and every ferry leave from here
The widest choice of long-term rentals on the island
cons: The waterfront is noisy and functional rather than pretty
Ferry traffic and arrivals at all hours in summer

name: Naoussa
tagline: The old fishing harbour, and the island's best eating and nightlife
description: A whitewashed harbour village on the north coast, built around a small Venetian breakwater, now the island's most fashionable address with the best restaurants and the summer bar scene. The lanes behind the harbour are genuinely lovely. It empties considerably from November but does not close entirely.
bestFor: Summer stays that want the restaurants, the bars and the prettiest streets
pros: The best restaurants and bars on the island
Beautiful lanes and a working fishing harbour
Beaches at Kolymbithres and Monastiri a short hop away
cons: The highest rents on Paros in season
Very crowded in July and August
Much of it shuts down in deep winter

name: Lefkes and the Inland Villages
tagline: Marble lanes in the hills, cool in summer and lived in
description: The old capital, set high in the interior among terraces and olive groves, with the Byzantine road running down towards the east coast. Lefkes and its neighbours Prodromos and Marpissa are working villages rather than resorts, noticeably cooler than the coast, and far cheaper for a long lease.
bestFor: Longer stays that want village life, cooler air and a proper local price
pros: Considerably cooler than the coast in summer
Long-term rents well below the harbours
Genuine village life that continues through winter
cons: A car or scooter is essential
Very few restaurants and no nightlife
Twenty minutes to the nearest beach

name: Golden Beach and Chrissi Akti
tagline: The windward east coast, where the surfing happens
description: The long sand beaches on the exposed eastern side, which the meltemi turns into one of the better windsurfing and kitesurfing spots in the Aegean. Accommodation is low-rise studios and small hotels strung along the coast road, aimed squarely at people who came for the wind and the water.
bestFor: Anyone here for the board rather than the town
pros: Reliable wind and a long sand beach
Relaxed and much less crowded than the north
cons: Twenty-five minutes by bus to Parikia
The same wind that makes it work makes it uncomfortable on shore

name: Aliki and the South
tagline: A quiet fishing village near the airport, family-paced
description: A small fishing settlement on the southern coast with a sheltered bay, a handful of tavernas on the water and a beach that stays calm when the meltemi is blowing on the other side of the island. It is quieter than anywhere else with a beach, and the airport is a few minutes away.
bestFor: Stays that want a calm beach, a taverna and no crowds at all
pros: Sheltered from the meltemi that batters the east coast
cons: Very little to do beyond the beach and the tavernas
Twenty minutes to Parikia for real shopping
